mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least three consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be positive due to lower real borrowing costs and increased equity discounting.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < mean(FEDFUNDS) over the past 12 months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-rate-cut average (t-test p > 0.05), or the rate remains above its long-run mean for >6 months without a subsequent positive return.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with falling unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which is associated with higher consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >5% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In 20 consecutive triggered months, SPX 20-day returns are negative or flat despite the labor signal, with a t-statistic < -1.96.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above trend for two consecutive months predicts higher corporate order backlogs and optimism about future demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > INDPRO_trend_avg for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In a 60-day window with INDPRO above trend, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative on average, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months reduces the Fed's disinflationary bias, lowering real rates and increasing equity valuations, which tends to produce negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 20 days following the trigger, SPX 20-day returns are consistently positive or the inflation signal reverses with no return benefit.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly ratio of residential mortgage applications (HOUST) exceeds its 12-month moving average, it indicates strong housing demand and accommodative credit conditions, which are associated with positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In 10 consecutive triggered windows, SPX 5-day returns are not positive or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% followed by a sustained rise in job openings (PAYEMS) suggests a tight labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and higher inflation expectations, often preceding negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In 20 triggered instances, SPX 20-day returns are not negative or the effect is not robust to out-of-sample retesting (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for more than six months, coupled with low industrial production (INDPRO), signals deflationary pressures that can depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0 for 6 consecutive months AND INDPRO < INDPRO_trend_avg for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 60 days post-trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not negative on average, or the interaction is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in retail sales (not directly observable in the given catalog, but as a proxy we use HOUST as a stand-in for consumer demand) accompanied by a decline in jobless claims (implied by UNRATE dynamics) predicts optimism about future demand, which tends to drive positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by >0.3 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In 20 triggered windows, SPX 20-day returns are not positive or the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05).
